title: An outside review of secret-protection-core 0.2.0 at cd06231 and its remediation

reviews.method: Source review of cd06231, with fmt, dprint, Clippy on the host and six targets, and the Linux suites.

reviews.snapshot: the remediation working tree on cd06231

releaseDecision.reason: The native runs on Linux ARM64, macOS and Windows must pass the acceptance criteria of AUD-017 and the findings below.

excluded: Native runs on systems other than Linux x86-64, which CI performs

checks.evidence: On Linux x86-64 with Rust 1.99.1 at the fix commit: `cargo fmt --check` for the crate and the fuzz targets, `dprint check`, Clippy with warnings denied for Linux x86-64, Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, WebAssembly, `armv5te-unknown-linux-gnueabi` and the fuzz targets, all 119 checks (53 unit tests, 33 isolation checks, 9 secret-memory checks and 24 worker checks), the stack tests in the release profile, rustdoc with warnings denied for the host, WebAssembly, Windows and macOS, the coverage recipe of docs/COVERAGE.md before the review of the remediation (94.55%, 3,710 of 3,924 lines) and `cargo audit` against the advisory database of 2026-11-24 for both lockfiles.

findings.title: A Windows worker cannot open its own first thread
findings.reproduction: Since 0.2.0 the parent creates an AppContainer worker's first thread with `THREAD_ACCESS`, one entry for OWNER RIGHTS. The worker's own `enter` opened every listed thread by number with `OpenThread(MAXIMUM_ALLOWED)`, its own included. An AppContainer's access check also needs an entry for its package SID, which that list lacks, so the open is expected to fail: `NoMemoryReading` refused, and every `Worker::start` on Windows refused.
findings.observed: Since 0.2.0 the parent creates an AppContainer worker's first thread with `THREAD_ACCESS`, one entry for OWNER RIGHTS. The worker's own `enter` opened every listed thread by number with `OpenThread(MAXIMUM_ALLOWED)`, its own included. An AppContainer's access check also needs an entry for its package SID, which that list lacks, so the open is expected to fail: `NoMemoryReading` refused, and every `Worker::start` on Windows refused.
findings.impact: Since 0.2.0 the parent creates an AppContainer worker's first thread with `THREAD_ACCESS`, one entry for OWNER RIGHTS. The worker's own `enter` opened every listed thread by number with `OpenThread(MAXIMUM_ALLOWED)`, its own included. An AppContainer's access check also needs an entry for its package SID, which that list lacks, so the open is expected to fail: `NoMemoryReading` refused, and every `Worker::start` on Windows refused.
findings.recommendedFix: `enter` sets and reads the access list of the calling thread through its pseudo handle, which needs no access check, as the integrity pass already did; other threads are still opened by number.
findings.requiredVerification: The Windows worker tests in native CI: a worker starts in its AppContainer and reports `NoMemoryReading` confirmed.

findings.title: macOS folder privacy misses symbolic links on the given path
findings.reproduction: On macOS `is_private` walked the folder's real parents through `..`. A symbolic link on the path as given, which another user owns or may replace, was not seen: `is_private` stayed true while that user could point the path the program writes by elsewhere.
findings.observed: On macOS `is_private` walked the folder's real parents through `..`. A symbolic link on the path as given, which another user owns or may replace, was not seen: `is_private` stayed true while that user could point the path the program writes by elsewhere.
findings.impact: On macOS `is_private` walked the folder's real parents through `..`. A symbolic link on the path as given, which another user owns or may replace, was not seen: `is_private` stayed true while that user could point the path the program writes by elsewhere.
findings.recommendedFix: `settled_on_the_way` follows the given path name by name, links included: every folder a name is looked up in must be the user's or root's, writable by others only with the sticky bit, with no access list for anyone; a name in such a shared folder and every link must be the user's or root's; at most 32 links. macOS only, as before; Landlock holds the folder itself.
findings.requiredVerification: A native macOS run of the folder role, which makes a folder through a link in a folder others may write in and expects `is_private` false.

findings.title: macOS reads a missing TMPDIR as file writes allowed
findings.reproduction: When `TMPDIR` named a folder that does not exist, the probe's exclusive creation failed with NotFound, which counted as not refused: `NoFileChanges` read Refused although the sandbox refuses writes. The error is on the safe side, a protection reported missing.
findings.observed: When `TMPDIR` named a folder that does not exist, the probe's exclusive creation failed with NotFound, which counted as not refused: `NoFileChanges` read Refused although the sandbox refuses writes. The error is on the safe side, a protection reported missing.
findings.impact: When `TMPDIR` named a folder that does not exist, the probe's exclusive creation failed with NotFound, which counted as not refused: `NoFileChanges` read Refused although the sandbox refuses writes. The error is on the safe side, a protection reported missing.
findings.recommendedFix: Only folders that exist are probed, each in turn: success means writes are allowed, a permission refusal means they are refused, any other error tries the next place, and none left reads Unknown. Test: on macOS the isolated role runs with `TMPDIR` naming a folder that does not exist and still reports `NoFileChanges` confirmed.
findings.requiredVerification: That test in a native macOS run.

findings.title: No native run on Windows, macOS and Linux ARM64 since 0.1.0, and untested paths
findings.reproduction: Windows, macOS and Linux ARM64 have run no test since 0.1.0, so AUD-016-SEC009 and the pending findings of AUD-017 wait. SGR mouse reports, `clear_stack` alone and a worker's request longer than its first 4 KiB buffer had no test.

findings.title: Unix hidden input keeps flow control and stripping, misreads a non-waiting input, and drains twice
findings.reproduction: The hidden settings left `IXON`, `IGNCR` and `ISTRIP` as found: Ctrl+S and Ctrl+Q stayed flow control, a terminal set to ignore carriage returns swallowed Enter, and one that strips the eighth bit changed non-ASCII keys. An input set not to wait (`O_NONBLOCK`) failed with a misleading message, `terminal_for` took Linux's access mode 3, which serves ioctls alone, for both reading and writing, and a first drain that failed was followed by a second one on the way out.
findings.observed: The hidden settings left `IXON`, `IGNCR` and `ISTRIP` as found: Ctrl+S and Ctrl+Q stayed flow control, a terminal set to ignore carriage returns swallowed Enter, and one that strips the eighth bit changed non-ASCII keys. An input set not to wait (`O_NONBLOCK`) failed with a misleading message, `terminal_for` took Linux's access mode 3, which serves ioctls alone, for both reading and writing, and a first drain that failed was followed by a second one on the way out.
findings.impact: The hidden settings left `IXON`, `IGNCR` and `ISTRIP` as found: Ctrl+S and Ctrl+Q stayed flow control, a terminal set to ignore carriage returns swallowed Enter, and one that strips the eighth bit changed non-ASCII keys. An input set not to wait (`O_NONBLOCK`) failed with a misleading message, `terminal_for` took Linux's access mode 3, which serves ioctls alone, for both reading and writing, and a first drain that failed was followed by a second one on the way out.
findings.recommendedFix: The hidden settings clear `BRKINT`, `IXON`, `IGNCR` and `ISTRIP` and read them back; an input set not to wait is refused before anything changes, and a drain that finds the input set so meanwhile reads it as empty; a descriptor counts for reading or writing only in that mode or read-write; the drain on the way out is armed only after the first one succeeded. Tests: keys arrive whole under those flags, a non-waiting input is refused, and a mode-3 descriptor is no terminal to use.
findings.requiredVerification: The Linux unit tests pass; the macOS run of the terminal role remains.

findings.title: A folder's path keeps a final `/` or `/.`
findings.reproduction: `WritableFolder::create` kept a final `/` or `/.` in the path it stores, after which the check that the path still leads to the folder followed a link at its last name.
findings.observed: `WritableFolder::create` kept a final `/` or `/.` in the path it stores, after which the check that the path still leads to the folder followed a link at its last name.
findings.impact: `WritableFolder::create` kept a final `/` or `/.` in the path it stores, after which the check that the path still leads to the folder followed a link at its last name.
findings.recommendedFix: The path is stored without them. Test: a folder made at `…/made/.` keeps `…/made`, byte for byte, and once the folder is moved away and a link to it put at `…/made`, the path no longer leads to it.
findings.requiredVerification: The unit test passes on Linux.

findings.title: A fork during the Landlock layer's TSYNC gives a child the layer without its record
findings.reproduction: Between `landlock_restrict_self` with TSYNC and the store of `LAYERED_PROCESS`, a fork on another thread gave a child the layer but no record of it; a later `enter_with_folders` there would report `FolderWrites` confirmed while the inherited layer refuses the writes.
findings.observed: Between `landlock_restrict_self` with TSYNC and the store of `LAYERED_PROCESS`, a fork on another thread gave a child the layer but no record of it; a later `enter_with_folders` there would report `FolderWrites` confirmed while the inherited layer refuses the writes.
findings.impact: Between `landlock_restrict_self` with TSYNC and the store of `LAYERED_PROCESS`, a fork on another thread gave a child the layer but no record of it; a later `enter_with_folders` there would report `FolderWrites` confirmed while the inherited layer refuses the writes.
findings.recommendedFix: Where an earlier secret or isolation put the gate of secret memory in place, the call holds it across the layer and its record, so such a fork waits; it never registers the gate itself, which among other threads would settle secret memory as unavailable for good. Without the gate, or when it stays busy past 100 ms, the window stays, as TECHNICAL.md says.
findings.requiredVerification: Review; the race is not reproducible in a test.

findings.title: Windows finds a console for `write_secret` by its mode
findings.reproduction: `write_secret` took standard output for a console only when `GetConsoleMode` succeeded, which needs the read right; a console open only for writing got UTF-8 bytes, which it shows in its code page. The review also named unchecked lengths of `GetTokenInformation` and an unsplit `WriteConsoleW`.
findings.observed: `write_secret` took standard output for a console only when `GetConsoleMode` succeeded, which needs the read right; a console open only for writing got UTF-8 bytes, which it shows in its code page. The review also named unchecked lengths of `GetTokenInformation` and an unsplit `WriteConsoleW`.
findings.impact: `write_secret` took standard output for a console only when `GetConsoleMode` succeeded, which needs the read right; a console open only for writing got UTF-8 bytes, which it shows in its code page. The review also named unchecked lengths of `GetTokenInformation` and an unsplit `WriteConsoleW`.
findings.recommendedFix: A console is a handle that `GetConsoleMode` accepts, or a character device for which it answers access denied, as a console open only for writing does; NUL, a file or a pipe answer otherwise and keep `WriteFile`. Not changed: a successful `GetTokenInformation` has written all it reports, and `WriteConsoleW` has had no 64 KiB limit since Windows 8, older than the policies this crate needs.
findings.requiredVerification: A native Windows run with a console.

findings.title: macOS access-list kinds, a split list in HISTORY.md, and CI without dprint and ARMv5
findings.reproduction: `listed_access` counted only allowing entries, so an entry of an unknown kind passed as granting nothing; a blank line split a list of HISTORY.md in two; CI ran neither `dprint check` nor Clippy for a 32-bit Linux without this crate's filter. The review also asked for `proc_pidinfo` to be retried on EINTR.
findings.observed: `listed_access` counted only allowing entries, so an entry of an unknown kind passed as granting nothing; a blank line split a list of HISTORY.md in two; CI ran neither `dprint check` nor Clippy for a 32-bit Linux without this crate's filter. The review also asked for `proc_pidinfo` to be retried on EINTR.
findings.impact: `listed_access` counted only allowing entries, so an entry of an unknown kind passed as granting nothing; a blank line split a list of HISTORY.md in two; CI ran neither `dprint check` nor Clippy for a 32-bit Linux without this crate's filter. The review also asked for `proc_pidinfo` to be retried on EINTR.
findings.recommendedFix: Every entry but a denying one counts as allowing; the second list has a heading of its own; CI installs dprint by its SHA-256 and checks the formatting, and `armv5te-unknown-linux-gnueabi` joins the targets that Clippy lints. Not changed: `proc_pidinfo` waits for nothing a signal could interrupt (CORE-54).
findings.requiredVerification: CI on the pushed commit; the access lists on macOS natively.

findings.title: A Unix worker that ends just after its shutdown wait counts as not ended
findings.reproduction: When the worker ended by itself after the first wait ran out and was collected before the kill, `pidfd_send_signal` answered ESRCH, `terminate` returned false, and `finish` reported the worker as not ended.
findings.observed: When the worker ended by itself after the first wait ran out and was collected before the kill, `pidfd_send_signal` answered ESRCH, `terminate` returned false, and `finish` reported the worker as not ended.
findings.impact: When the worker ended by itself after the first wait ran out and was collected before the kill, `pidfd_send_signal` answered ESRCH, `terminate` returned false, and `finish` reported the worker as not ended.
findings.recommendedFix: On Linux with a pidfd, `terminate` counts ESRCH as ended, so the second bounded wait reports the exit; macOS and the POSIX fallback have no stable handle to ask. Test: a child collected before the kill counts as ended.
findings.requiredVerification: The unit test passes on Linux.

findings.title: A protected stack's size, a work area's debug text after fork, and the worker's buffer order
findings.reproduction: `run_on_protected_stack` raised the size to `PTHREAD_STACK_MIN` after rounding it to pages, which leaves it unaligned where that minimum is no whole page; the `Debug` text of a `WorkArea` read its bytes, which ends a child of `fork`; a worker allocated a larger request buffer before giving back the old one, holding both.
findings.observed: `run_on_protected_stack` raised the size to `PTHREAD_STACK_MIN` after rounding it to pages, which leaves it unaligned where that minimum is no whole page; the `Debug` text of a `WorkArea` read its bytes, which ends a child of `fork`; a worker allocated a larger request buffer before giving back the old one, holding both.
findings.impact: `run_on_protected_stack` raised the size to `PTHREAD_STACK_MIN` after rounding it to pages, which leaves it unaligned where that minimum is no whole page; the `Debug` text of a `WorkArea` read its bytes, which ends a child of `fork`; a worker allocated a larger request buffer before giving back the old one, holding both.
findings.recommendedFix: The minimum comes first, then whole pages; `Debug` takes the length the pages record, without reaching them; the old buffer is dropped first. Test: a child of `fork` formats its parent's work area.
findings.requiredVerification: The fork test passes on Linux; the stack size on a 16 KiB page needs a native macOS run.

observations.title: The steps of a TSYNC entry are not one atomic step
observations.reproduction: A thread that puts in a seccomp filter of its own between `share_filters` and the filter's TSYNC makes the call stay short of the whole process, which reports `WholeProcess` refused; a thread with a Landlock layer of its own has it replaced. observations.title: A thread an AppContainer worker starts after its default list changed cannot be opened by number
observations.reproduction: Such a thread starts with the restricted list, as the first one does, so the worker cannot open it by number; one that appears between the change and the walk makes `NoMemoryReading` read as not confirmed and the start fail. It fails closed, needs a thread started in that instant, and TECHNICAL.md says so.
